provenance: SME base prompt Agents 1-2 Inputs sections; MAI-35277 Inputs section; field groups and labels corroborated by the mock UI field pickers on screen 1.

population.label: Indication / disease
population.definition: The disease or condition being treated.

population.label: Age group
population.definition: Age band of the licensed population.

population.label: Prior therapy / line
population.definition: Treatment the patient has already received, and at which line.

population.label: Performance status
population.definition: Functional status scale, e.g. ECOG or Karnofsky.

population.label: Other characteristics
population.definition: Any other population characteristic not covered by another field.
population.note: Free text. The scope-boundary agent normalises its content into named facets. This is where an axis with no dedicated field (e.g. a treatment-free interval) currently has to live - see OPEN QUESTION in ARCHITECTURE.md.

population.label: Is the intended-to-treat population the same?
population.definition: Declares whether the intended-to-treat population differs from the licensed population, and how.
population.note: When this states a difference, Input Structuring emits a SECOND population object (SME Agent 2 step 8).

population.label: Disease subtype / histology
population.note: CONFIRMED only when the exact subtype is named in the indication wording; otherwise NOT PROVIDED. Never guess the statistically more common subtype.

population.label: Orphan / rare-disease
population.definition: Whether the condition is designated orphan or rare.
population.note: When set, 'Rare Diseases' is ALWAYS added as an additional therapeutic area (SME Agent 5).

population.label: Therapeutic area
population.definition: One of the 11 fixed areas the guideline source list is organised around.
population.note: MAY be inferred by Input Structuring only when the disease singularly belongs to one area.

population.label: Treatment setting / intent
population.definition: Setting and treatment intent, e.g. curative, palliative, maintenance, adjuvant.

intervention.label: Product name (INN)
intervention.definition: The assessed product, expected as the International Nonproprietary Name.

intervention.label: Therapeutic class / mechanism
intervention.definition: The INTERVENTION's pharmacological class and mechanism.
intervention.note: NEVER inferred by Input Structuring (SME Agent 2 rule 5). NEVER written onto a comparator - a comparator's class comes from the comparator's own INN.

intervention.label: Generic name
intervention.definition: Generic name, where the product name given was a brand name.

intervention.label: Line of therapy
intervention.definition: The line at which the intervention is intended to be used.

intervention.label: Pivotal trial identifier(s)
intervention.definition: Registry identifiers for the pivotal trial(s), e.g. NCT number or EU CT number.
intervention.note: The most precise retrieval key available. Used directly against the trial-registry APIs.

intervention.label: Claimed / anticipated indication wording
intervention.definition: The indication wording the manufacturer will claim.
intervention.note: Defines the scope boundary when no EMA label exists yet - essential for a pre-approval product, which is the product's primary use case.
